To solve this problem, I need to work backwards from 5 B.C. to find the year when a child born that year would turn 15.

In B.C. dating, years count backwards from 1 B.C. to 5 B.C., and then from 1 A.D. onwards.

If a child is born in 5 B.C., they would turn 15 years old 15 years later.

5 B.C. + 15 years = ?

Let me count:
- 5 B.C. → 4 B.C. (1 year)
- 4 B.C. → 3 B.C. (2 years)
- 3 B.C. → 2 B.C. (3 years)
- 2 B.C. → 1 B.C. (4 years)
- 1 B.C. → 1 A.D. (5 years) - Note: There is no year 0 in the traditional calendar
- 1 A.D. → 2 A.D. (6 years)
- 2 A.D. → 3 A.D. (7 years)
- 3 A.D. → 4 A.D. (8 years)
- 4 A.D. → 5 A.D. (9 years)
- 5 A.D. → 6 A.D. (10 years)
- 6 A.D. → 7 A.D. (11 years)
- 7 A.D. → 8 A.D. (12 years)
- 8 A.D. → 9 A.D. (13 years)
- 9 A.D. → 10 A.D. (14 years)
- 10 A.D. → 11 A.D. (15 years)

So a child born in 5 B.C. would turn 15 in 11 A.D.

<answer>11 A.D.</answer>
